findings.reason: the project's binding evidence rule puts a contour panel in every record that produces a terminal forward state, so the node would close a record of solved states without the instrument the rule exists to require on a batching change whose failure mode is numeric.
findings.text: §4's done-when delivers terminal forward states (the solo positive control and the qualified width-16 and width-64 batched states) but requires the record only to carry converged flags, residuals and walls, no poloidal flux panel; §1(3) and §3(3) each require a line-contour panel of the terminal state on the stored state's shared levels with both null sets and the batch's positive control is itself a state no panel shows

findings.reason: deleting the prescription leaves the same endpoint while removing a constraint the worker cannot check before building it, and an infeasible widening otherwise forces a deviation the plan does not permit, at 6 hours of elevated-risk work.
findings.text: §4 says the section "repairs that route under the existing batched entry, and widens that entry to take the plan's request and return, per state, the receipt fields of the unbatched public solve": that names a function to extend and fixes the interface it must grow into, which is incorrect plan content. The endpoint alone should state that one call accepts the public solve request and returns per-state receipt fields; whether the existing batched entry can be widened or a second surface is needed is an interface guess the reviewer would have to test against `solve_batch` (`nova/equilibrium/forward.py:3220`), which today vmapps `_solve_accelerated` over arrays and carries no request pytree
